title: Spurs Take Control Early, Cruise Past Trail Blazers Behind De'Aaron Fox; 5 Key Takeaways - NewsBreak
text:
By Eddie Bitar ,
1 minutes ago The San Antonio Spurs didn’t overcomplicate things; they executed better than the Portland Trail Blazers in the 112-101 victory on Wednesday night. Leading for 86% of the game and building a lead as large as 17, San Antonio dictated the tempo and never truly let Portland settle in.
This wasn’t a flashy win, but it was a professional one. The Spurs didn’t need Victor Wembanyama on the evening as De’Aaron Fox led the charge with 25 points to give the team their 61st victory in what has been an extremely impressive season. Here are the five key takeaways of this game.
1. De’Aaron Fox Set The Tone De’Aaron Fox led the way with 25 points on 10-20 shooting, adding 7 assists and 3 steals in a performance that balanced scoring and playmaking.
He controlled the pace, especially in the halfcourt, where his ability to collapse the defense created opportunities for others. Even when Portland made brief pushes, Fox responded by either getting to his spots or setting up teammates.
It was more than the numbers – it was about control. Fox dictated how the game was played.
2. Spurs’ Depth Flipped The Game San Antonio’s bench outplayed Portland’s, and it wasn’t particularly close. Keldon Johnson poured in 20 points on 8-15 shooting, while Carter Bryant added 17 points, including 5-6 from three.

That second unit production created separation. While Portland struggled to generate consistent offense off the bench, the Spurs extended leads and maintained pressure.
San Antonio had three bench players finish with a +9 or better plus-minus, highlighting how impactful that group was throughout the game.
3. Free Throw Disparity Helped Decide It The numbers at the line tell a huge part of the story. The Spurs went 15-19 from the free-throw line (78.9%), while the Blazers managed just 5-10 (50%).
That’s a 10-point difference in a game decided by 11 – and it reflects aggression. San Antonio consistently attacked and earned trips to the line, while Portland settled for tougher looks.
In games where possessions are relatively even, that kind of efficiency gap becomes a backbreaker.
4. Portland Had Firepower, But No Control The Portland Trail Blazers had strong individual performances, particularly from Deni Avdija, who led all scorers with 29 points on 13-21 shooting.
Scoot Henderson added 20 points, and Toumani Camara chipped in 18 with efficient shooting. On paper, that’s enough to compete.
But the problem was cohesion. Portland shot just 32.4% from three and 50.0% from the line, and their 16 turnovers repeatedly stalled momentum. The offense had moments – just not consistency.
5. Defensive Activity Helped Spurs End It San Antonio’s defense wasn’t dominant in one area – it was disruptive across the board. They recorded 13 steals and forced 16 turnovers, turning defense into offense when needed.
Dylan Harper contributed across the stat sheet with 13 points, 6 rebounds, 4 assists, and 2 steals, while multiple Spurs players were active in passing lanes.
Even when Portland found success inside (58 points in the paint), the Spurs countered with timely stops and transition opportunities that kept the game out of reach.
